analysis.title: 3Q26 Small Cap Market Overview
key_insights: Small caps lagged in 3Q26 as investors concentrated on a small cohort of large AI-related names. The Russell 2000 fell 7.2%, Russell 2500 fell 6.4%, Russell Midcap fell 3.0%, while the S&P 500 gained 2.3%.
Year-to-date, small caps still lead large caps: Russell 2000 +13.7% and Russell 2500 +14.9% versus S&P 500 +12.7%. Value outperformed growth in the quarter across capitalizations.
US real GDP grew 2.5% in Q1 and 2.2% in Q2 2026, driven by business investment and consumer spending. The Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate is 3.6% for Q3.

US consumer prices rose 3.4% over the latest 12 months, with the energy component up 16.3%. Energy prices remain elevated because of supply shocks from the war in Iran, and resilient growth has pushed inflation above target in much of the world.
The FOMC voted unanimously in mid-September to raise the fed funds target by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%. The dot plot suggests one more hike before year end.

The 10-year Treasury yield finished the quarter near 5.3% and the 2-year at 4.9%, levels not seen consistently since before the global financial crisis. Yields have risen steadily since the Iran war began at the end of February.

The author says it is unclear whether a prolonged hiking cycle has begun. Additional hikes are possible, but the lack of formal Fed guidance under Chair Warsh makes the path hard to assess. The need to roll over a large primary deficit at higher rates constrains how far the Fed can raise rates.

Smaller companies rely more on short-term floating-rate debt than large caps, so tighter policy could materially affect them. The author notes that rising rates alongside a robust economy have historically not hurt small cap returns.

Published forecasts show Russell 2000 earnings growth of 86% in 2026 and 44% in 2027, versus 35% and 15% for the S&P 500. The author would not be surprised if small caps benefit if the Iran war ends and energy prices and inflation ease.
The manager rotated out of technology and industrials after a strong first half and into healthcare, energy and idiosyncratic opportunities, while keeping valuations cheaper than the market.

earnings_insights: Published forecasts (LSEG I/B/E/S, as of Sept 4, 2026) show consensus earnings growth of 86% for the Russell 2000 in 2026 and 44% in 2027, versus 35% and 15% for the S&P 500.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth accelerated in the first half after limited growth in Q4 2025.
Growth was driven by business investment and consumer spending.
A running model estimate, not an official forecast, pointing to further acceleration.
Inflation is above target, driven by a 16.3% rise in the energy component.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Energy is the main driver of headline inflation.
The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points unanimously. The dot plot suggests one more hike before year end.
The level has not been seen consistently since before the global financial crisis and weighs on small caps.

risk_factors: Persistent inflation and rising bond yields are a headwind for small caps.
Small caps rely more on short-term floating-rate debt, so further Fed hikes could raise their funding costs.
The lack of formal Fed guidance under Chair Warsh makes the policy path hard to assess.
The government's need to roll over a large primary deficit at higher rates limits the Fed's flexibility.
The Iran war may not conclude, leaving energy prices and inflation elevated.
vol_and_positioning: Market leadership in 3Q26 was concentrated in a small cohort of large AI-related names, while smaller stocks fell out of favor.
geopolitical: War in Iran caused energy supply shocks. Economies have adjusted by sourcing crude from other regions, drawing on strategic and commercial inventories, and through some demand destruction and substitution.
Gulf oil exports have recovered through rerouting efforts and increasing dark transits, but energy prices remain elevated.
The author's constructive case for small caps depends partly on a successful conclusion to the Iran war in the coming months.

tension_points.bull_case: Rising rates alongside a robust economy have historically not hurt small cap returns, because strong activity supports fundamentals. Russell 2000 earnings are forecast to grow 86% in 2026 and 44% in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Small caps rely more on short-term floating-rate debt, so tighter policy could have a material impact. The Fed may hike further and yields are at multi-year highs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A prolonged hiking cycle with further hikes beyond the one the dot plot signals before year end, or the Iran war continuing to keep energy prices and inflation elevated.

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong earnings growth and a robust economy have historically supported small caps even as rates rise.
theme_stances.evidence: Rising rates coincidental with a robust economic backdrop have not historically been an impediment

theme_stances.key_argument: Additional hikes are possible but the lack of formal guidance makes the path difficult to assess.
theme_stances.evidence: the deliberate lack of formal Fed guidance under the Warsh regime
